questions.question: TR52 divides GDP into seven pillars, but this report provides guidance on only the first four. Which set is exactly the four pillars TR52 covers?

options.A: Stability, Qualification/Validation, Distribution Control Management, Continuous Improvement
options.B: Stability, Distribution Control Management, Performance Management, Supply Chain Partner Management
options.C: Distribution Control Management, Performance Management, Continuous Improvement, Import/Export Compliance
options.D: Stability, Performance Management, Qualification/Validation, Import/Export Compliance

questions.explanation: TR52 covers the four pillars Stability, Distribution Control Management, Performance Management, and Supply Chain Partner Management; Qualification/Validation, Continuous Improvement, and Import/Export Compliance are left to other PDA technical reports.

questions.topic: Responsibility — who the guidance applies to
questions.question: A third-party logistics provider (3PL) believes the TR52 GDP guidance is a matter for pharmaceutical companies only and does not concern them. Under TR52 §1.2, which statement is most accurate?

options.A: It applies only to companies holding the marketing authorization; other parties decide for themselves under contract whether to follow it
options.B: It applies only to manufacturers and their own warehouses; external logistics providers are outside its scope
options.C: It applies to all parties that handle, store, or transport regulated products, including manufacturers, marketing authorization holders, 3PLs, wholesalers, and transport carriers
options.D: It applies only to wholesalers and carriers, because only they come into direct contact with the product

questions.explanation: TR52 §1.2 states explicitly that the guidance applies to all parties involved in the handling, storage, and/or transportation of regulated products, and 3PLs are included. The other options narrow the scope too much.

questions.question: In the TR52 glossary, which inventory control method does First Expiration, First Out (FEFO) refer to?

options.A: The material received earliest is shipped first
options.B: The customer whose order was received earliest is shipped first
options.C: The material with the lowest lot number is shipped first
options.D: The material with the shortest remaining shelf life is distributed first

questions.explanation: FEFO determines shipping order by remaining shelf life, so that the product that expires first is distributed first; it is not based on receipt date or order sequence.
questions.reference: PDA TR52 §2.0 Glossary: First Expiration, First Out (FEFO)

questions.question: According to the TR52 glossary, which cites the ICH Q1A(R2) definition, what is Mean Kinetic Temperature (MKT)?

options.A: A single derived temperature which, if maintained over a defined period, affords the same thermal challenge as the actual range of temperatures experienced (using the Arrhenius equation)
options.B: The arithmetic mean of all temperature readings over a period, used to represent the overall temperature level of that period, without regard to degradation kinetics or the magnitude and frequency of temperature fluctuations
options.C: The highest temperature recorded over a period, used to represent worst-case thermal exposure and as the upper limit for deciding whether to scrap product
options.D: The midpoint of the upper and lower limits of the labeled storage range, used to set warehouse temperature targets in place of the actual temperature records of each batch

questions.explanation: ICH Q1A(R2) defines MKT as a single derived temperature whose thermal challenge equals that of the actual range of high and low temperatures experienced, calculated with the Arrhenius equation. It is not a simple average, a maximum, or a range midpoint.
questions.reference: PDA TR52 §2.0 Glossary: Mean Kinetic Temperature (MKT)

questions.question: Which statement about how the TR52 glossary distinguishes Logistics Service Providers (LSP or 3PL) from Transportation Service Providers (TSP) is correct?

options.A: LSPs physically transport the goods and bear transport responsibility; TSPs only handle paperwork and customs clearance and never touch the goods
options.B: LSPs are freight forwarders, customs brokers, and the like that assist in shipping and may not touch the product; TSPs are the companies that physically transport the product
options.C: They mean the same thing and differ only in US versus European usage, so their responsibilities need not be distinguished under GDP requirements
options.D: LSP refers specifically to warehouse operators with temperature control capability; TSP refers specifically to air cargo companies operating international routes

questions.explanation: The glossary defines LSPs/3PLs as freight forwarders and customs brokers that assist with shipment but may not physically handle the product; TSPs are the companies that actually transport the product. The statement "LSPs physically transport the goods and TSPs only handle paperwork" reverses the two roles.
questions.reference: PDA TR52 §2.0 Glossary: Logistics Service Providers (LSP or 3PLs); Transportation Service Providers (TSP)

questions.question: TR52 §3.1.1 mentions that storage temperature monitoring may use "continuous monitoring." Which best matches its description?

options.A: A qualified active monitoring system with automatic alarms that notifies relevant personnel when the temperature deviates
options.B: Personnel manually recording and signing the temperature each shift, with a supervisor compiling and reviewing it the next day, as an alternative to continuous monitoring
options.C: Downloading data logger data once a month, reviewing it afterward for out-of-range readings, and recording the results in a monthly report
options.D: Performing a temperature distribution test once a year and using its results as evidence that temperatures were acceptable all year, with no other monitoring

questions.explanation: The key to continuous monitoring is an active, qualified system with automatic alarms that notifies at the moment a deviation occurs rather than discovering it afterward; disposition-oriented review of the temperature data is still required.

questions.question: A product's shipping temperature range is wider than the long-term storage conditions on its label. Under TR52 §3.1.2, when is this acceptable?

options.A: It is not acceptable; shipping must always fully match the labeled storage range, even when supported by stability data and temperature-excursion studies, unless the regulatory authority separately approves it batch by batch
options.B: It is acceptable if the carrier agrees and signs a service agreement, with no separate stability or scientific justification needed to support widening the shipping temperature range
options.C: It is acceptable if the supplier provides an MKT calculation, with no other stability data needed and no need to consider domestic or foreign regulatory requirements for shipping conditions
options.D: There are stability data or scientific rationale showing that quality is not affected, and applicable regulations are met; the range is determined by temperature-excursion studies

questions.explanation: TR52 permits shipping outside the labeled storage conditions provided there are stability data or a scientific/technical rationale showing that quality is not affected, and regulatory requirements are met. The option "if the supplier provides an MKT calculation" is wrong because MKT may be used only when the degradation curve follows Arrhenius predictions and the regulatory authority allows it.

questions.question: On arrival of a monitored cold-chain shipment, the data logger shows that the labeled storage conditions or the established shipping range were exceeded. Under TR52 §3.1.2, what must the investigation at least establish?

options.A: Whether the carrier should pay compensation, whether to change carriers, and whether the affected product is to be sold at a discount to secondary channels or returned to the customer at a discount
options.B: How long the excursion lasted, the identity of the driver, and whether the DEA and local police must be notified as required with a written statement from the driver
options.C: The root cause of the excursion, necessary corrective actions (if applicable), and the potential impact on the product (which must be documented)
options.D: Whether the excursion was recorded by the data logger, whether the logger needs recalibration, and whether to change the design of the outer packaging, refrigerant configuration, and carrier route

questions.explanation: TR52 requires that an excursion investigation establish the root cause, necessary corrective actions, and potential product impact, and the product impact must be documented; the other options are commercial or peripheral matters, not the prescribed focus of the investigation.

questions.question: Quality wants to use MKT to evaluate the effect of a shipping temperature excursion on the product. Under TR52 §3.1.2, under what conditions might MKT be an acceptable method?

options.A: It can be used whenever continuous temperature records are available, without verifying that degradation behavior follows the Arrhenius equation
options.B: The degradation curve established from stability data follows the Arrhenius equation predictions, and the local regulatory authority allows the use of MKT
options.C: It can directly replace stability data for any refrigerated product, with no need to explain to the regulatory authority and no need to evaluate the duration or peak temperature of the excursion
options.D: If the calculated MKT does not exceed the labeled upper limit, the product is considered unaffected, with no need to evaluate the duration of the excursion

questions.explanation: MKT has two prerequisites: the degradation curve follows Arrhenius predictions (supported by actual stability data), and the local regulatory authority permits its use. Temperature records or product category alone are not sufficient support.

questions.question: A product must temporarily leave the refrigerated environment during pack-out. Under TR52 §3.1.3, how should the Time Out of Refrigeration (TOR) limit be set?

options.A: It must be defined and controlled, justified with appropriate stability data, and consistent with the service level or quality agreement
options.B: It may be set from the warehouse's past operating experience without stability data, but must be approved in writing by the warehouse manager
options.C: Adopt the carrier's standard handling time without separate verification, as long as the carrier provides its internal SOP
options.D: The allowable time is determined by the data logger sampling interval and adjusted each time for seasonal ambient temperature

questions.explanation: TR52 requires that time limits such as TOR be defined and controlled, supported by stability data, and consistent with the service level or quality agreement; any time range outside the labeled temperature or humidity must be supported by data. Experience or sampling intervals are not a basis.

questions.question: Commercial product should normally be received into the warehouse only after release. Under TR52 §3.2.3.2, in which situation may product in quarantine status be received and shipped?

options.A: As long as the goods carry a quarantine label, warehouse staff may decide for themselves, and the WMS status record and warehouse signature are added after release
options.B: For any customer, provided the customer agrees in writing to bear the release risk, with the agreement retained by both the sales department and the customer
options.C: Transfers between sites or between a manufacturer's third-party warehouses, with no shipment to customers before release, documented approval by both quality units, and the WMS restricting authority to change status
options.D: Only for product whose final testing is complete but whose report is not yet signed off, with oral confirmation by the warehouse manager noted on the shipping document and later ratified by the customer's quality unit before receipt

questions.explanation: TR52 allows this under these conditions: transfer between sites or between a manufacturer's third-party warehouses, controls preventing shipment before release, documented approval by the quality units of both the sender and receiver (for example, a quality agreement), and a warehouse management system that ensures correct status and controlled authority.

questions.question: A warehouse discovers suspected counterfeit product in the distribution network. Under TR52 §3.2.3.4, which disposition is correct?

options.A: First return it to the supplier and obtain a written reply, then notify the regulatory authority and marketing authorization holder as appropriate, keeping correspondence records
options.B: Destroy it on site and keep destruction records and photographs, with approval by warehouse quality staff only, without notifying any party or the original manufacturer
options.C: Label it and hold it in a quarantine area until the next routine audit, then report it to the regulatory authority together with other deviations, with no shipment in the interim
options.D: Segregate it from saleable product in a restricted, controlled area clearly marked as not for sale, and immediately notify the regulatory authority and the marketing authorization holder

questions.explanation: Counterfeit product must be segregated from saleable product in a restricted area and marked not for sale, with the regulatory authority and the original manufacturer's marketing authorization holder notified immediately, and handled per national or local regulations. Delayed reporting or self-destruction does not meet the requirement.

questions.question: A customer returns a lot of cold-chain drugs with intact, unopened outer packaging, but the customer returned it after taking it into its own inventory. Under TR52 §3.2.8, how should this return be viewed?

options.A: It does not meet the conditions for restocking evaluation, because documentation must show the product was not taken into the customer's inventory in order to maintain chain of custody
options.B: As long as it is unopened and in good condition, it may be restocked with QA sign-off and flagged in the system as a customer return lot with the return reason
options.C: It may be restocked, but an additional temperature mapping is required, and the customer must provide temperature evidence and receiving records for the return period
options.D: It may be restocked if the return shipment had a data logger throughout and the records show the labeled range was not exceeded, with QA review

questions.explanation: One of the restocking evaluation conditions TR52 lists is documentation showing the product was not taken into the customer's inventory, in order to maintain chain of custody; the text also notes that many companies do not restock cold-chain returns because of inconsistent control of return shipping. Intact packaging and a logger cannot make up for this requirement.

questions.question: Under TR52 §3.2.5, which statement about monitoring locations and pre-loading inspection of temperature-controlled vehicles is correct?

options.A: Monitoring only one point in the center of the compartment, covering the whole transit period, is enough; pre-loading checks may be confirmed verbally without records, with documented checks added afterward only if an excursion is found in transit
options.B: Monitor at least the front and rear of the vehicle, covering the whole transit period; before loading, check cleanliness and temperature setting (if applicable) and document it
options.C: Monitor only the temperature at the rear door; pre-loading checks are performed and documented only when a problem was found on a previous shipment
options.D: Monitoring the front and rear of the vehicle is needed only on long-distance transport; pre-loading checks may be confirmed by driver signature instead

questions.explanation: TR52 requires monitoring that covers at least the front and rear of the vehicle and supports the length of the transit time, and requires vehicle cleanliness and temperature setting to be checked and documented before loading and transport. A single point, after-the-fact checks, or verbal confirmation are not sufficient.

questions.question: What does TR52 §3.2.4.2 require of the system that controls and maintains product status (such as on test, approved, quarantined, restricted)?

options.A: The warehouse manager adjusts status flexibly according to shipping needs, with the quality unit confirming afterward
options.B: Only written procedures and manual log records are needed, with no computerized system validation and no change control, and status changes approved by the warehouse manager
options.C: It must be a validated system, subject to appropriate change control, with only appropriate quality personnel able to change product status
options.D: Status needs updating only at the annual inventory count, and in between warehouse staff mark it in the system on their own based on experience

questions.explanation: The product status control system must be validated, placed under change control, and restrict status changes to appropriate quality personnel; computerized systems also require qualification and validation. Letting warehouse staff adjust status flexibly would undermine release control.

questions.topic: Self-inspection and closed loop supply chain
questions.question: TR52 §3.3.2 says that self-inspection can form a "closed loop supply chain." What does this mean?

options.A: All returns are closed back to the original warehouse for handling and no longer flow into other channels, with the original warehouse responsible for destruction, records, and annual reconciliation
options.B: The entire supply chain uses only the manufacturer's own vehicles and warehouses, with no outsourcing to any external third-party service provider, to avoid blurred responsibility
options.C: Once a supplier signs a quality agreement, the manufacturer no longer needs to audit, and the supplier's annual self-declaration of compliance suffices, with CAPA follow-up waived
options.D: Self-inspection covers the quality systems of internal supply chain partners, monitors GDP implementation, and triggers CAPA and effectiveness follow-up

questions.explanation: TR52 uses closed loop supply chain to describe how a manufacturer, through self-inspection, understands and continuously monitors its supply chain partners and operations and achieves continuous improvement through CAPA. It has nothing to do with owning vehicles, closing the returns loop, or waiving audits.

questions.topic: Management review vs business review agenda
questions.question: Comparing the agenda lists of Management Review Meetings in TR52 §3.3.3 and Business Review Meetings in §3.5, which item appears only in Business Review Meetings?

options.A: Quality audit results
options.B: Storage and transportation requirements for new products
options.C: Status of corrective and preventive actions (CAPA)
options.D: Performance metrics (actual versus target)

questions.explanation: Audit results, performance metrics, and CAPA status are discussed in both meetings; only Business Review Meetings additionally list the storage and transportation requirements of new products.
questions.reference: PDA TR52 §3.3.3 vs §3.5 (Business Review Meetings: New product requirements)

questions.question: A company is evaluating whether a new transportation service provider can support GDP compliance. Under TR52 §3.4.1, which is a key area the selection process should include?

options.A: The carrier's safety records
options.B: The carrier's annual revenue, financial growth rate over the past three years, and market share ranking
options.C: The carrier's ownership structure, the listing status of its parent company, and its merger and acquisition history
options.D: The carrier's total headcount and the average tenure of management

questions.explanation: The selection areas TR52 lists include the carrier's safety records, regulatory certifications (such as VAWD, ISO), operating policies and procedures, vehicles and equipment, and security. Revenue, ownership, and headcount are not on the list and do not indicate GDP capability.

questions.topic: Quality audit approach and N/A justification
questions.question: Under TR52 §3.4.2, which statement about quality system audits of supply chain service providers is correct?

options.A: On-site audits are always required, and sections that do not apply may simply be skipped, without being recorded or any rationale provided
options.B: The service provider decides for itself which sections are not applicable, and the manufacturer need not ask for a rationale or review it separately
options.C: A risk-based on-site visit or questionnaire approach may be used; sections of the audit checklist that are not applicable (N/A) must be justified
options.D: Questionnaires are limited to low-risk suppliers, and N/A sections may be skipped only after prior approval by the regulatory authority

questions.explanation: TR52 allows risk-based on-site or questionnaire audits and requires that non-applicable sections be marked N/A with a justification (for example, storage of expanded polystyrene and corrugated cardboard does not need a temperature profile).

questions.question: Under TR52 §3.4.3, how should responsibility for the various aspects of GDP be assigned among the parties in the supply chain?

options.A: Each carrier is responsible for its own scope, with no written agreement needed, and responsibility is negotiated individually with the manufacturer when problems arise
options.B: A quality agreement is signed once and remains valid long-term without updates, even if the scope of service or the subcontractors have changed, unless a major deviation occurs
options.C: The 3PL allocates it uniformly to its downstream subcontractors, and the manufacturer keeps only final shipment and payment records and confirms at an annual meeting, with no written agreement with subcontractors
options.D: The manufacturer or marketing authorization holder ensures that responsibilities are assigned and carried out, formalized through covenants or Quality Agreements and updated periodically

questions.explanation: TR52 states that the manufacturer and/or marketing authorization holder is responsible for ensuring that each aspect is assigned and implemented, and for putting this in writing with all third parties through quality agreements, which must be updated periodically. Responsibility cannot rest on verbal agreement or be passed on through a 3PL.

questions.topic: Checklist F — calibration of temperature recorders
questions.question: When the TR52 Good Storage and Shipping Practices Checklist (F, storage temperature control) asks about the calibration frequency of temperature recording devices, what is the point of the check?

options.A: At least once a year, against an acceptable standard (for example, NIST)
options.B: Once a quarter, with warehouse staff comparing against another uncalibrated thermometer themselves and logging it
options.C: Once every three years, in step with the mapping review, with the supplier's factory certificate replacing on-site calibration
options.D: Recalibrated before every use, with the supplier comparing against an internally established reference standard

questions.explanation: Checklist F asks whether temperature recording devices are calibrated at least annually against an acceptable standard (such as NIST), and requires calibration records for each device. The three-year cycle applies to the mapping review, not to calibration.

questions.question: An auditor uses Checklist F to ask about temperature mapping of the warehouse's controlled temperature areas. What approach does the checklist take to periodic review of the mapping results?

options.A: Remap every year without fail, regardless of whether the warehouse layout and equipment have changed
options.B: Remap every five years, with no review in between, except when the regulatory authority requires it sooner or the warehouse has a major equipment or layout change
options.C: Include the mapping review in the validation plan, with a review every three years to determine whether remapping is needed
options.D: Review only when equipment is relocated or fails; otherwise the mapping results may be used indefinitely

questions.explanation: Checklist F asks whether there is a plan to include temperature mapping in the validation plan, with a review every three years to determine whether remapping is necessary; mapping itself should also cover seasonal extremes and peak business periods. It is not a fixed annual repeat, nor a review only after an event occurs.

questions.topic: Checklist E — storage distance from walls
questions.question: During a warehouse walk-through, for product stored along an exterior wall, what clearance from the wall does Checklist E (product storage) ask about?

options.A: 1 to 3 inches
options.B: 6 to 18 inches
options.C: 24 to 36 inches
options.D: No clearance is needed, as long as the product is off the floor on pallets

questions.explanation: Checklist E asks whether product stored along exterior walls keeps a clearance of 6 to 18 inches (to allow inspection and pest control); a separate question covers keeping product off the floor on pallets or racks, and the two requirements differ.

questions.topic: Checklist K vs other temperature sections
questions.question: An auditor wants to confirm how a supplier manages dry ice, how long it can be stored, and whether insulated shipping containers have been tested for seasonal extremes and different transport modes. Which section of the checklist should be used?

options.A: F. Temperature Control/Calibration Storage
options.B: L. Carrier Transportation Temperature Controls (carrier transportation temperature controls, including vehicles, cargo compartments, driver cabs, and long-haul transfer terminals)
options.C: G. Temperature Control Distribution (distribution temperature control, including loading docks and staging areas)
options.D: K. Insulated Shipping Systems (ISS) Transportation Temperature Controls

questions.explanation: Section K deals specifically with the selection of insulated shipping systems, testing for seasonal extremes and transport modes, refrigerant conditioning time, and the management and replenishment of dry ice; section L addresses the carrier's vehicles, routes, and transport monitoring, and section F covers warehouse temperature control.

questions.question: An auditor finds customer returns mixed with approved stock in the same area. Under the checks of Checklist M (customer returns), how should returns be managed?

options.A: Customer returns must be physically segregated from approved stock, with QA checking that the product is in its original condition; restocking or destruction must be approved by QA
options.B: They may be mixed with approved stock in the same area and identified by serial number, with restocking approved by the warehouse manager and logged in the system
options.C: The sales department decides whether to restock and notes it in the ERP, with the quality unit spot-checking return records only at the annual audit
options.D: Check only quantity and visible damage and book them in immediately, with no need to confirm temperature during transport and no QA review or approval

questions.explanation: Checklist M requires that returns be inspected by appropriate personnel (including original condition, seals, and whether temperature was maintained), physically segregated from approved stock, and covered by a documented system ensuring QA reviews repackaging, restocking, or destruction. Mixing them and letting the sales department decide are contrary to this.

questions.question: Of the global regulations and guidelines listed in TR52 §5.1, which one was issued by the World Health Organization (WHO)?

options.A: Guidelines for Temperature Control of Drug Products during Storage and Transportation (GUIDE-0069)
options.B: Annex 5, Good Distribution Practices (GDP) for Pharmaceutical Products (2005)
options.C: Guide to Control and Monitoring of Storage and Transportation Temperature Conditions for Medicinal Products and Active Substances
options.D: Perishable Cargo Regulations

questions.explanation: The WHO document is Annex 5, GDP for Pharmaceutical Products (2005); GUIDE-0069 is from Health Canada, the other temperature control guide is from the Irish Medicines Board, and the Perishable Cargo Regulations are from IATA.

questions.question: TR52 §5.1 cites ICH Q8, Q9, and Q10. What is the subject of each?

options.A: Q8 Pharmaceutical Quality System, Q9 Pharmaceutical Development, Q10 Quality Risk Management
options.B: Q8 Quality Risk Management, Q9 Pharmaceutical Development, Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System
options.C: Q8 Pharmaceutical Quality System, Q9 Quality Risk Management, Q10 Pharmaceutical Development
options.D: Q8 Pharmaceutical Development, Q9 Quality Risk Management, Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System

questions.explanation: The references list Q8 Pharmaceutical Development, Q9 Quality Risk Management, and Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System. The other options merely scramble the pairing of the three.

questions.question: TR52 §5.2 lists PDA TR46 under Selected Publications. What is its subject?

options.A: Stability testing guidance for new drugs to support distribution, covering the design of accelerated and long-term studies
options.B: Guidance on temperature-controlled drug products for maintaining the quality of temperature-sensitive drugs in the shipping environment, covering qualification of insulated containers
options.C: Last Mile: Guidance for GDP for pharmaceutical products to the end user
options.D: Quality audit methods for supply chain partners, including auditor qualifications and the format requirements of audit reports

questions.explanation: TR46 is Last Mile: Guidance for GDP for Pharmaceutical Products to the End User. Stability testing to support distribution is TR53, and the quality of the shipping environment for temperature-sensitive drugs is TR39.

questions.question: Which organization issued the Perishable Cargo Regulation (2009) listed in TR52 §5.1?

options.A: IATA (International Air Transport Association)
options.B: ICH (International Council for Harmonisation)
options.C: WHO (World Health Organization)
options.D: Health Canada

questions.explanation: The Perishable Cargo Regulation is issued by the International Air Transport Association (IATA), and it is the rule TR52 expects temperature-controlled products shipped internationally to be labeled in accordance with.

questions.question: A company's product will be distributed in the EU and the US. Which pair of documents in the TR52 §5.1 list corresponds to those markets, respectively?

options.A: EU: WHO Annex 5 Good distribution practices for pharmaceutical products (TRS 957); US: Health Canada GUIDE-0069 Good distribution practices for medical devices and drugs
options.B: EU: Guidelines on Good Distribution Practice of Medicinal Products for Human Use (94/C 63/03); US: CFR Part 211
options.C: EU: ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System guideline; US: IATA Perishable Cargo Regulation
options.D: EU: the Irish Medicines Board distribution guidance document; US: ICH Q9 Quality Risk Management

questions.explanation: The EU document is the EU GDP guideline (94/C 63/03), and the US document is Food and Drugs CFR Part 211 (with FD&C Act provisions as well). The other options mismatch the issuing bodies and markets.
